s: Sakra is a destroyer of towns
q: the destroyer of towns

s: Sakra is a performer of a hundred sacrifices
q: the performer of a hundred sacrifices

s: Sakra is a thousand-eyed one
q: the thousand-eyed one, Maghavan

s: Sakra is a lord of the thirty-two thousand celestial abodes
q: the lord of the thirty-two thousand celestial abodes

s: Sakra rides the elephant Airavata
q: the bestrider of the elephant Airavata

s: Sakra belongs to Saudharma Kalpa (resides there)
q: this Sakra was in the Saudharma Kalpa

s: Sakra resides in Saudharma Avatamsaka (celestial abode)
q: in the celestial abode Saudharma Avatamsaka

s: Sakra sits on the throne Sakra (in Sudharman)
q: in the council-hall Sudharman, on his throne Sakra

s: Sakra commands the gods (supreme command, government, management, guidance, direction, sovereign power, and generalship)
q: he who exercises and maintains the supreme command, government, management, guidance, direction, and sovereign power and generalship over the thirty-two thousand gods of the celestial abodes

s: Sakra orders Harinegamesi (to transfer Mahâvîra's embryo)
q: Therefore, go now and remove the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra from the brahmanical part, &c., and place the embryo of the

s: Harinegamesi is a divine commander of the foot troops
q: Harinegamesi, the divine commander of the foot troops

s: Harinegamesi transfers Mahâvîra's embryo (from Devânandâ's womb to Trisalâ's womb)
q: the embryo of the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra was, on the command of Sakra, safely removed by Harinegamesi from the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ to that of the Kshatriyânî Trisalâ

s: Kshatriyânî Trisalâ is a Kshatriyânî
q: the Kshatriyânî Trisalâ

s: Kshatriyânî Trisalâ belongs to the Vâsishtha gotra
q: the Kshatriyânî Trisalâ of the Vâsishtha gotra

s: Kshatriyânî Trisalâ is wife of Siddhârtha
q: wife of the Kshatriya Siddhârtha of the Kâsyapa gotra

s: Kshatriyânî Trisalâ has embryo the embryo (placed in the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ)
q: the embryo of the Kshatriyânî Trisalâ he placed in the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ

s: Siddhârtha is a Kshatriya
q: the Kshatriya Siddhârtha

s: Siddhârtha belongs to the Kâsyapa gotra
q: the Kshatriya Siddhârtha of the Kâsyapa gotra

s: Siddhârtha is husband of Kshatriyânî Trisalâ
q: wife of the Kshatriya Siddhârtha of the Kâsyapa gotra

s: Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra has life moments in Uttaraphalgunî (descent, conception, transfer, birth, renunciation, and attainment of Kevala)
q: the five (most important moments of whose life happened) when the moon was in conjunction with the asterism Uttaraphalgunî; to wit, in Uttaraphalgunî he descended (from heaven), and having descended (thence), he entered the womb (of Devânandâ); in Uttaraphalgunî he was removed from the womb (of Devânandâ) to the womb (of Trisalâ); in Uttaraphalgunî he was born; in Uttaraphalgunî, tearing out his hair, he left the house and entered the state of houselessness; in Uttaraphalgunî he obtained the highest knowledge and intuition, called Kevala

s: the transfer of Mahâvîra's embryo is performed by Harinegamesi (on Sakra's command)
q: the embryo of the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra was, on the command of Sakra, safely removed by Harinegamesi

s: the transfer of Mahâvîra's embryo moves from the womb of Devânandâ
q: removed by Harinegamesi from the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ

s: the transfer of Mahâvîra's embryo moves to the womb of Devânandâ (the embryo of Trisalâ is placed there in exchange)
q: the embryo of the Kshatriyânî Trisalâ he placed in the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ

s: embryo of the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra (in Trisalâ's womb) is placed in the womb of Devânandâ (during the transfer)
q: the embryo of the Kshatriyânî Trisalâ he placed in the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ

s: the Arhats are born in high families (past, present, and future)
q: For indeed Arhats, Kakravartins, Baladevas, and Vasudevas, in the past, present, and future, are born in high families, noble families, royal families

s: the Arhats are removed to high families (when conceived in low families)
q: to cause the Arhats and Bhagavats to be removed from such-like low, mean, &c., families, to such-like high, noble, &c., families

s: the Ginas are conquerors who have conquered fear
q: reverence to the Ginas who have conquered fear.

s: the Tîrthakaras are perfectly-enlightened ones
q: to the Âdikaras, the Tîrthakaras, the perfectly-enlightened ones

s: the Tîrthakaras number twenty-three (already appeared before Mahâvîra)
q: after twenty-one Tîrthakaras of the race of Ikshvâku and of the Kâsyapa gotra, and two of the race of Hari and of the Gautama gotra, on the whole twenty-three Tîrthakaras had appeared

s: the gods include Suras (as a designation)
q: the chief of the Suras

s: Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra obtains final liberation in Svâti
q: But in. Svâti the Venerable One obtained final liberation.

s: Gambûdvîpa contains Bharatavarsha
q: in the continent of Gambûdvîpa, in Bharatavarsha

s: Kundagrâma has part the brahmanical part of Kundagrâma
q: in the brahmanical part of the town Kundagrâma

s: Kundagrâma has part the Kshatriya part of Kundagrâma
q: to the Kshatriya part of the town Kundagrâma

s: the Kshatriya part of Kundagrâma contains the Kshatriyânî Trisalâ (at the house of the Kshatriya Siddhârtha)
q: he went to the Kshatriya part of the town Kundagrâma, to the house of the Kshatriya Siddhârtha, where the Kshatriyânî Trisalâ dwelt

s: Uttaraphalgunî is a asterism
q: when the moon was in conjunction with the asterism Uttaraphalgunî

s: Kevala is a highest knowledge and intuition (infinite, supreme, unobstructed, unimpeded, complete, and perfect)
q: the highest knowledge and intuition, called Kevala, which is infinite, supreme, unobstructed, unimpeded, complete, and perfect

s: the fourteen great dreams include an elephant
q: To wit: An elephant, a bull, a lion, the anointing (of the goddess Srî), a garland, the moon, the sun, a flag, a vase, a lotus lake, the ocean, a celestial abode, a heap of jewels, and a flame.

s: the fourteen great dreams include a bull
q: To wit: An elephant, a bull, a lion, the anointing (of the goddess Srî), a garland, the moon, the sun, a flag, a vase, a lotus lake, the ocean, a celestial abode, a heap of jewels, and a flame.

s: the fourteen great dreams number fourteen (illustrious, beautiful, lucky, blest, auspicious, and fortunate)
q: having seen the following fourteen illustrious, beautiful, lucky, blest, auspicious, fortunate great dreams

s: Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra descends from Pushpottara (the great Vimâna, all-victorious and all-prosperous)
q: descended from the great Vimâna, the all-victorious and all-prosperous Pushpottara

s: the elephant Airavata is ridden by Sakra
q: the bestrider of the elephant Airavata

s: the throne Sakra is used by Sakra (in the council-hall Sudharman)
q: on his throne Sakra

s: Mahâvîra's final liberation occurs in Svâti
q: But in. Svâti the Venerable One obtained final liberation.

s: Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra takes form in the womb of Devânandâ (initially, in the brahmanical part of Kundagrâma)
q: the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra took the form of an embryo in the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ

s: Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra is transferred to the womb of the Kshatriyânî Trisalâ (from the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ)
q: the embryo of the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra was, on the command of Sakra, safely removed by Harinegamesi from the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ to that of the Kshatriyânî Trisalâ

s: Mahâvîra's conception occurs in the womb of Devânandâ (before the transfer)
q: the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra took the form of an embryo in the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ

s: monks collect alms within a Yogana and a Krosa (during the Paggusan)
q: During the Paggusan monks or nuns are allowed to go and return, for the sake of collecting alms, not farther than a Yogana and a Krosa (from their lodgings).

s: nuns collect alms within a Yogana and a Krosa (during the Paggusan)
q: During the Paggusan monks or nuns are allowed to go and return, for the sake of collecting alms, not farther than a Yogana and a Krosa (from their lodgings).

s: Âkârya directs food giving sick man (during the Paggusan)
q: During the Paggusan the Âkârya will say, 'Give, Sir!' Then he is allowed to give (food to a sick brother), but not to accept himself.

s: Âkârya directs food acceptance sick man (during the Paggusan)
q: If the Âkârya says, 'Accept, Sir!' then he is allowed to accept (food), but not to give.

s: monks are restricted from frequently taking nine drinks (when hale, healthy, and of a strong body during the Paggusan)
q: Monks or nuns who are hale and healthy, and of a strong body, are not allowed during the Paggusan frequently to take the following nine drinks: milk, thick sour milk, fresh butter, clarified butter, oil, sugar, honey, liquor, and meat.

s: nuns are restricted from frequently taking nine drinks (when hale, healthy, and of a strong body during the Paggusan)
q: Monks or nuns who are hale and healthy, and of a strong body, are not allowed during the Paggusan frequently to take the following nine drinks: milk, thick sour milk, fresh butter, clarified butter, oil, sugar, honey, liquor, and meat.

s: Paggusan dietary restrictions include nine drinks (milk, thick sour milk, fresh butter, clarified butter, oil, sugar, honey, liquor, and meat)
q: the following nine drinks: milk, thick sour milk, fresh butter, clarified butter, oil, sugar, honey, liquor, and meat.

s: monks eat one meal a day (during the Paggusan)
q: During the Paggusan a monk eats only one meal a day, and should at one fixed time frequent the abodes of householders for the sake of collecting alms

s: monks obtain alms (by frequenting householders' abodes at one fixed time during the Paggusan)
q: During the Paggusan a monk eats only one meal a day, and should at one fixed time frequent the abodes of householders for the sake of collecting alms

s: Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra commences Paggusan (when a month and twenty nights of the rainy season had elapsed)
q: In that period, in that age the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra commenced the Paggusan when a month and twenty nights of the rainy season had elapsed.

s: monks accept all permitted drinks (when eating one meal every day during the Paggusan)
q: A monk who during the Paggusan eats one meal every day, is allowed to accept all (permitted) drinks.

s: monks accept hot pure water (when keeping still more protracted fasts during the Paggusan)
q: A monk who during the Paggusan keeps still more protracted fasts, is allowed to accept only one kind of drink: hot pure water.

s: monks restrict visits to certain houses (during the Paggusan)
q: During the Paggusan monks or nuns who restrict their visits to certain houses may go to a place where rice is cooked, if it is the seventh house from that where they are lodged.

s: monks use alms-bowl (during the Paggusan)
q: During the Paggusan a monk who uses an alms-bowl is not allowed to frequent the abodes of householders for the sake of collecting alms if it rains fast, but he is allowed to do so if it rains but little

s: hollow of the hand holds alms (for a monk collecting alms during the Paggusan)
q: During the Paggusan a monk who collects alms in the hollow of his hand

s: rain restricts alms collection monks (when falling even as a fine spray during the Paggusan)
q: During the Paggusan a monk who collects alms in the hollow of his hand, is not allowed to frequent the abodes of householders, &c., if rain, even in the form of a fine spray, falls down.

s: monks require permission from teacher (before collecting alms during the Paggusan)
q: He is not allowed to go without asking leave of the teacher, or sub-teacher, or religious guide, or Sthavira, or head of the Gana, or Ganadhara, or founder of the Gana, or whom else he regards as his superior

s: monks require permission for medical cure (during the Paggusan)
q: The same rule applies if a monk wants to undergo some medical cure.

s: monks require permission for exalted penance (during the Paggusan)
q: Also if he wants to do some exalted penance.

s: monks must have three lodging-places (during the Paggusan)
q: During the Paggusan monks or nuns should have three lodging-places; (two) for occasional use, which must be inspected; one for constant use, which must be swept.

s: nuns must have three lodging-places (during the Paggusan)
q: During the Paggusan monks or nuns should have three lodging-places; (two) for occasional use, which must be inspected; one for constant use, which must be swept.

s: Paggusan conduct rules prohibit harsh words (after the commencement of the Paggusan)
q: During the Paggusan monks or nuns should not use harsh words after the commencement of the Paggusan

s: Paggusan conduct rules require forgiveness (when quarrels, disputes, or dissensions occur)
q: If, during the Paggusan, among monks or nuns occurs a quarrel or dispute or dissension, the young monk should ask forgiveness of the superior, and the superior of the young monk.

s: peace is the essence of monastic control
q: Peace is the essence of monachism.

s: monks must inspect three spots where to ease nature (during the Paggusan, especially in the rainy season)
q: During the Paggusan monks or nuns must always inspect three spots where to ease nature; not so in the summer and winter, as in the rainy season.

s: monks must have three pots (during the Paggusan)
q: During the Paggusan monks or nuns must have three pots, one for ordure, one for urine, and a spitting-box.

s: nuns must have three pots (during the Paggusan)
q: During the Paggusan monks or nuns must have three pots, one for ordure, one for urine, and a spitting-box.

s: Ganadharas commence Paggusan (when a month and twenty nights of the rainy season had elapsed)
q: As the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra commenced the Paggusan when a month and twenty nights of the rainy season had elapsed, so the Ganadharas commenced the Paggusan when a month and twenty nights of the rainy season had elapsed.

s: disciples of the Ganadharas commence Paggusan (following the Ganadharas)
q: As the Ganadharas have done, so the disciples of the Ganadharas have done.

s: Paryushanâkalpa is a Lecture (with its application, argumentation, information, text, meaning, and examination of the meaning)
q: he proclaimed again and again the Lecture called Paryushanâkalpa with its application, with its argumentation, with its information, with its text, with its meaning, with both text and meaning, with the examination of the meaning.

s: Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra proclaims Paryushanâkalpa (in Râgagriha, in the Kaitya Gunasilaka)
q: In that period, in that age the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra, in the town of Râgagriha, in the Kaitya Gunasilaka, surrounded by many monks and nuns, by many men and women of the laity, by many gods and goddesses, said thus, spoke thus, declared thus, explained thus; he proclaimed again and again the Lecture called Paryushanâkalpa

s: Sthaviras commence Paggusan (following the disciples of the Ganadharas)
q: As they have done, so the Sthaviras have done.

s: Nirgrantha Sramanas commence Paggusan (in the present time, following the Sthaviras)
q: As they have done, so do the Nirgrantha Sramanas of the present time.

s: monks regard residence as extending a Yogana and a Krosa (during the Paggusan)
q: Monks or nuns during the Paggusan are allowed to regard their residence as extending a Yogana and a Krosa all around, and to live there for a moderate time.

s: nuns regard residence as extending a Yogana and a Krosa (during the Paggusan)
q: Monks or nuns during the Paggusan are allowed to regard their residence as extending a Yogana and a Krosa all around, and to live there for a moderate time.

s: embryo of the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra (in Trisalâ's womb) is a embryo
q: the embryo of the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra was removed from the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ of the Gâlandharâyana gotra to that of the Kshatriyânî Trisalâ of the Vâsishtha gotra

s: the fourteen great dreams is seen by Kshatriyânî Trisalâ
q: having seen the following fourteen, &c. (see § 3), dreams, viz. an elephant, &c. (see § 4), she awoke.

s: the fourteen great dreams includes first dream elephant (first dream)
q: Then Trisalâ saw in her first dream a fine, enormous elephant

s: the fourteen great dreams includes second dream bull (second dream)
q: Then she saw a tame, lucky bull

s: the fourteen great dreams includes third dream lion (third dream)
q: Then she saw a handsome, handsomely shaped, playful lion

s: the fourteen great dreams includes Srî (fourth dream)
q: Then she, with the face of the full moon, saw the goddess of famous beauty, Srî

s: the fourteen great dreams includes fifth dream flower garland (fifth dream)
q: Then she saw, coming down from the firmament, a garland charmingly interwoven with fresh Mandâra flowers.

s: the fourteen great dreams includes sixth dream moon (sixth dream)
q: And the moon: white as cow-milk, foam, spray of water, or a silver cup, glorious, delighting heart and eyes, full, dispelling the compact darkness of the thickest wilderness

s: the fourteen great dreams includes seventh dream sun (seventh dream)
q: Then she saw the large sun, the dispeller of the mass of darkness

s: the fourteen great dreams includes eighth dream flag (eighth dream)
q: Then she saw an extremely beautiful and very large flag

s: the fourteen great dreams includes ninth dream vase (ninth dream)
q: Then she saw a full vase of costly metal

s: embryo of the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra (in Trisalâ's womb) belongs to Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra
q: the embryo of the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra was removed from the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ of the Gâlandharâyana gotra to that of the Kshatriyânî Trisalâ of the Vâsishtha gotra

s: the fourteen great dreams includes Lotus Lake (tenth dream)
q: Then she saw a lake, called Lotus Lake, adorned with water lilies.

s: the fourteen great dreams includes milk-ocean (eleventh dream)
q: Then she whose face was splendid like the moon in autumn, saw the milk-ocean

s: the fourteen great dreams includes twelfth dream celestial abode (twelfth dream)
q: Then she saw a celestial abode excelling among the best of its kind, like the lotus (among flowers).

s: the fourteen great dreams includes thirteenth dream jewel heap (thirteenth dream)
q: Then she saw an enormous heap of jewels containing Pulaka, Vagra, Indranîla, Sasyaka, Karketana, Lohitâksha, Marakata, Prabâla, Saugandhika, Sphatika, Hamsagarbha, Añgana, and Kandrakânta.

s: the fourteen great dreams includes fourteenth dream fire (fourteenth dream)
q: And a fire. She saw a fire in vehement motion, fed with much-shining and honey-coloured ghee, smokeless, crackling, and extremely beautiful with its burning flames.

s: mothers of Tîrthakaras see the fourteen great dreams (when a famous Arhat enters the womb)
q: Every mother of a Tîrthakara sees these fourteen dreams in that night in which the famous Arhat enters her womb.

s: embryo of the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra (in Trisalâ's womb) is removed from the womb of Devânandâ
q: the embryo of the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra was removed from the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ of the Gâlandharâyana gotra to that of the Kshatriyânî Trisalâ of the Vâsishtha gotra

s: embryo of the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra (in Trisalâ's womb) is placed in Kshatriyânî Trisalâ (in her womb)
q: the embryo of the Venerable Ascetic Mahâvîra was removed from the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ of the Gâlandharâyana gotra to that of the Kshatriyânî Trisalâ of the Vâsishtha gotra

s: Brâhmanî Devânandâ is a Brâhmanî
q: the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ of the Gâlandharâyana gotra

s: Brâhmanî Devânandâ belongs to Gâlandharâyana gotra
q: the womb of the Brâhmanî Devânandâ of the Gâlandharâyana gotra
